task.question: Who ousted Sussan Ley in February 2026 in Australian politics?
task.evidence: February 13 – Sussan Ley, the first female leader of the Liberal Party of Australia, was ousted by Angus Taylor.

answer:
Sussan Ley was ousted as the leader of the Liberal Party of Australia by Angus Taylor on February 13, 2026, during a leadership spill. Taylor won the leadership contest with a vote margin of 34 to 17. 

FINAL: Angus Taylor.

messages.content:
A leadership spill was held on 13 February 2026 to elect the leader of the Liberal Party of Australia, and by virtue, the leader of the Opposition. Angus Taylor was elected, defeating incumbent leader Sussan Ley. A spill for the deputy leadership was held concurrently, with Jane Hume being elected, defeating incumbent deputy leader Ted O'Brien.
Taylor, a leading member of the National Right party faction, resigned from Ley's shadow cabinet on 11 February, following his declaration that Ley was not "in a position to lead the party as it needs to be led". The spill motion was subsequently launched by Jess Collins and Phillip Thompson. Taylor announced his candidacy for the leadership on the morning of 12 February.
Following previous Liberal leader Peter Dutton's defeat in his own seat at the 2025 election, Sussan Ley was appointed as the acting leader of the Liberal Party, until a leadership election could be held.
The election was contested by Ley and Angus Taylor, with Ley defeating Taylor, 29 votes to 25.
Three outgoing Senators (Hollie Hughes, Linda Reynolds, David Fawcett) and the provisional winner of Bradfield, Gisele Kapterian, were allowed to vote in this leadership election. Hughes and Reynolds publicly endorsed Ley for leader and Kapterian identified as a moderate. Kapterian would end up narrowly losing Bradfield to Nicolette Boele on a later recount. This meant that Ley's narrow win over Taylor would likely have been even narrower had the moderate outgoing Senators and Kapterian not been present. Ley's internal mandate as party leader was therefore seen as weak from the very beginning of her tenure.

Sussan Ley was ousted as the leader of the Liberal Party of Australia by Angus Taylor on February 13, 2026, during a leadership spill. Taylor won the leadership contest with a vote margin of 34 to 17. 

FINAL: Angus Taylor.
